Every number below is quoted from its deck.

03 — The method

What all four decks did the same way

Four different boards, four different sizes — and one identical planning sequence. If you are scoping your own odd-form automation, this is the order of work that produced every table in this series.

01

Sort the part list by package

Bulk, tube, tape, tray, reel — the package decides the feeder, and the feeder decides the machine. Parts that resist the sort are flagged for the bench, not forced into a cell.

02

Audit the clinch per part

Which legs must survive the wave with a hook? Which must stay straight — ceramic, magnetic, press-fit? The answer splits cam cells from vision cells, and the deck marks it row by row.

03

Balance cells to one cycle

Types per head, heads per cell, cells per line — divided until every station lands on the same cycle. The five-cell cases all prove it: identical cycles, no waiting heads.

04

Publish the arithmetic

3600 ÷ (insertion time × pieces + board change) per panel format. The decks print their formula; this series prints theirs. A vendor who cannot show the division is showing a brochure.

05

Sample on your board

Your components, your panel, the factory cell — acceptance on your product before the crate closes. Every case here started as a board in a padded envelope.

06

Keep the honest notes

Where a deck disagrees with itself — per-station times versus summary tables — both numbers are printed. Where it publishes nothing, this series computes and labels, never guesses.

05 — FAQ

Questions the series raises

Why publish customer solution decks at all?
Because the odd-form market runs on claims nobody can check. Each case here is traceable to a deck we produced for a real part list — customer names withheld, engineering facts published, computed values labelled.
Which case is closest to my board?
If your through-hole list is wide (fifteen-plus types), start with the five-cell case. If it is focused but mixed in package, the single cell. If terminals dominate, the DD-8600 specialist. If some parts must not be bent, the cam-plus-vision line.
Can these lines be mixed or grown?
The platform is modular by design: heads per cell, cells per line, feeders per head. The single-cell case becomes the five-cell case by adding what the part list earned — not by replacing the machine.
What do the lines cost?
Prices are quoted per part list, never per brochure. Send the board and the BOM — the evaluation (sort, clinch audit, station plan) is free until a sample run ships.
